subject: Spatial Fay-Herriot model - Symmetric matrix is not symmetric in cholesky_decompose

messages.author: 74cad518e374c928
messages.subject: Spatial Fay-Herriot model - Symmetric matrix is not symmetric in cholesky_decompose
parts:
Dear All,

first of all I would like to thank Stan development team for… Stan. :) It is really great, especially that I am starting my journey with bayesian models.

The problem that I have ran into is modelling spatial small area estimation model, in particular spatial Fay-Herriot model (SAE package vignette, page 14). 

In fact, there are two problems that I am struggling with:
  1. Matrix (that can be found below) that should be symmetric is not symmetric when it is decomposed by cholesky_decompose and therefore the model is not fitting correctly
  2. For big matrices the code is really slow (probably due to the crossprod and inverse of the spatial (sparse) matrix.

The spatial matrix is given by the following equation:

And the covariance matrix is then equal to:

Sigma =V_{u1} + diag_matrix(phi)

where phi are known sampling variances. Please find the example code below:


data(grapes)       # Load data set
data(grapesprox)   # Load proximity matrix 
grapes10 <- grapes[1:10,] ## first 10 obs for fast computation
grapesprox[grapesprox>0] <- 1
spatMat <- grapesprox[1:10,1:10]/rowSums(grapesprox[1:10,1:10])

data_in <- list(N = nrow(grapes10),
                Y = grapes10$grapehect,
                K = 3,
                X = model.matrix(~ area + workdays,grapes10),
                samperr = grapes10$var,
                S = spatMat,
                I = diag(nrow = nrow(grapes10)))

model <- 
  "
data { 
 int<lower=1> N;  
 vector[N] Y;  
 vector[N] samperr; 
 int<lower=1> K;  
 matrix[N, K] X;  
 matrix<lower=0,upper=1>[N, N] S;  
 matrix[N, N] I;  
} 

parameters { 
 vector[K] b;  # fixed effects 
 real<lower=0> sd_1;  # RE standard deviation 
 real rho;
} 
transformed parameters { 
 vector[N] eta;
 matrix[N,N] A;
 matrix[N,N] Sigma;
 matrix[N,N] Spatial;
 matrix[N,N] chol_Sigma;
 eta <- X * b; 
 A <- I - rho*S;
 Spatial <- inverse_spd( crossprod(A));
 Sigma <- sd_1*Spatial + diag_matrix(samperr);
 chol_Sigma <- cholesky_decompose(Sigma);
} 
model { 
 # prior specifications 
 sd_1 ~ cauchy(0,5); 
 rho ~ normal(0,1);
 # likelihood contribution 
 Y ~ multi_normal_cholesky(eta, Sigma); 
} 
"

fit <- stan(model_code = model, 
            data= data_in,
            pars = c('sd_1','rho','b','Sigma'),
            include = TRUE,
            thin = 10,
            cores = 4)

Exception thrown at line 27: cholesky_decompose: A is not symmetric. A[1,3] = -3.01171e+08, but A[3,     1
Exception thrown at line 27: cholesky_decompose: A is not symmetric. A[1,7] = 1.09371e+07, but A[7,1     1
Exception thrown at line 27: cholesky_decompose: A is not symmetric. A[5,10] = 1.44741e+07, but A[10     1
Exception thrown at line 27: cholesky_decompose: A is not symmetric. A[5,9] = -2.21306e+07, but A[9,     1
If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified.


I would appreciate any comments.
